questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have tried to learn spanish before the mobility and it was crucial for the exchange that it took place in a spanish speaking country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Almost everyone I encountered were very helpful, friendly and willing to teach me both academic and culture aspects of the everyday living. To me this was the best part of my overall experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of information, but not necessarily the information I needed. I didn't get an exact schedule before my arrival and had to wait a few days, even after arrival. It all worked out though so it didn't turn out to be a big deal, but it would have been nice with a programme.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did have an appointment with a secretary at the university on the first day. I got the opportunity to ask questions and I got the impression that there was some very genuine intentions helping me get started, but unfortunately it didn't work out until some days later. Again - didn't turn out to be a problem.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was fine at the university, but I had to go to the hospital and I think the first days/weeks was the hardest part of the stay. I had to ask around in the morning for the doctor I was supposed to follow and could really have used a small tour, an intro to the hospital or something like that.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing through a friend from home for the first month, and rented an airbnb for the last 2,5 month. So for me it was quite easy, but it was both lucky (the first month) and very expensive (the last 2,5). I guess it is easy to find housing if you can pay for it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: No problem for me! Everyone in my building was so sweet and my roommate the first month was also very easy going and helpful. Oviedo is not that big and you can easily get around even if you dont live super close to campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I am not sure. I wanted to bring my dog and that was not possible through the housing available for students, so I had to find something myself. I guess this wont be a problem for most students.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: easy, I did it the first day.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had an appointment the first day, ad registrated

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A secretary helped me

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I didn't have classes, only clinical rotations.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make an appointment in advance.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Good, almost everyone made an effort to educate me.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: clinical rotations for 11th semester medicine.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: My experience, compared to clinical rotations in Copenhagen, was that there was more time for teaching and education and doctors were more inclined to take the time needed to explain a case. Maybe they had more time, but at least this was my experience.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: clinical rotations.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: none really

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Most was less expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very satisfied. I could do almost every sport I liked. Biking, trail running, hiking, yoga ect.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was what to me seemed like endless Erasmus activities. I didn't join but there was both sports events (volley, hiking, kayaking, surfing), dining (tapas nights), culture trips to other cities and parties and social gatherings.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Race biking. Northern spain has a great culture for biking. it feels very safe and the scenery was wonderful. 
Also museums and and local festivities were very interesting.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: All of it. Go to the mountains, go to the beach. Visit other cities, it is both easy and cheap by bus. Cathedrals and museums and great for rainy days. But mostly I would recommend engaging in an everyday, do what the locals do and enjoy what they enjoy.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Meal hours was the hardest, but other than that it was quite easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: They were quite good at inviting me and I actually didn't have to do much myself to socialize.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none, I enjoyed most differences.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The way almost everyone was welcoming and wanted you to have a nice stay. This was altogether the best part about the whole stay.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: learn spanish, engage in local activities and festivities, make local friends

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: just want to emphasize how much it helped me knowing a little spanish before hand.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: again, getting to know people

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: getting started

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
